findings.reason: the accessor's signature and the handover node's scope both change once the mint's actual need (transformed values + raw time) is stated, and naming pulse_mint as a second resolver tells the author to extend the owner once rather than migrate one site and leave the other.
findings.text: the plan (plan.html §6, the observation-time-alignment paragraph) claims the new `VirtualZarrView` untransformed accessor is "the one both are meant to share", but `_served_entries` resolves a rule twice already: it takes transformed canonical values through `view.for_target(...)` (`imas_ambix/data/pulse_mint.py:203`) and separately the raw time base through `read_channel(...)` (`imas_ambix/data/pulse_mint.py:209`, `imas_ambix/data/eddb.py:280`), so it needs a *time-base* accessor beside transformed values, not an *untransformed-values* accessor; the same rule→source resolution is re-implemented at `imas_ambix/data/virtual_zarr.py:124` (`__getitem__` opens `rule.source_group`/`rule.source_array`) and at `imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py:759` (`read_signal_map_observation`, which the section migrates) — the ownership census is `VirtualZarrView` as the owner, with `pulse_mint._served_entries` and `read_signal_map_observation` as the two resolvers, and the plan has named only one of them for migration

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new behaviour (request-type dispatch, batch framing, the grid writer, the rule-to-source accessor) is hidden behind one extractor method and one view accessor, not spread across per-case wrappers; the request/record/refusal triple mirrors the existing `ChannelRequest`/`ChannelRecord`/`ChannelRefusal` shape because the key differs `(shot, record)` vs `(shot, category, dname)`, which is a data-shape necessity rather than surface for its own sake.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan leaves two rule-to-source resolvers in the tree and misstates the accessor as the surface both share; the census and the mismatch are in the finding below.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every section that adds surface names in its own text what it retires or why nothing can be. §7 retires three pin constants and their re-export for one machine-keyed table; §6 retires `read_catalogue_observation` for `read_signal_map_observation`; the §6 EQDB types retire nothing "because no equilibrium-database request type exists"; a transport failure stays `EddbRemoteError` and §6 adds no refusal family, consistent with the supplied `refusal_families 0`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design cites the mechanisms it extends and opens them: the §6 EQDB transport extends `imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py` (`SshTransport`, `RemoteEddbExtractor`) rather than a parallel ssh path, the sign scorer reuses `imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py score_convention`, the comparator reuses `imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py judge_geometry`, and the machine registry extends `imas_ambix/gs/machine_identity.py default_registry`; `grep -rni eqdb imas_ambix/` returns nothing, so the transport adds no duplicate of an existing reader.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the §6 untransformed accessor on `VirtualZarrView` is justified in its own text: the existing `__getitem__`/`for_target` apply the compiled transform, which carries the assumed +1 sign the section exists to measure, so the reader cannot be served by the transformed path and the view, which already owns rule→source resolution (`imas_ambix/data/virtual_zarr.py:124`), is where the raw read belongs.
